taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO and Flora of North America accept Ludwigia repens J.R.Forst.; the later Ludwigia repens Sw. is a different illegitimate homonym.
look_here_first: Look for creeping aquatic stems that root at the nodes, with opposite glossy elliptic-to-obovate leaves. In flower, confirm the small axillary yellow Ludwigia flower rather than relying on submerged habit alone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — a peer-reviewed San Marcos River aquatic-plant survey lists Ludwigia repens as native; Joey's Hays County source video independently shows it in the river. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County Onagraceae index includes an herbarium specimen of L. repens. Williamson — UT PRC Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed county treatment.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: The Hays decision uses a native-status river survey rather than inferring nativity from aquarium occurrence.

best_field_traits: aquatic perennial forming loose creeping mats
short-petioled glossy elliptic to obovate blades
creeping/submerged habit unlike erect Ludwigia octovalvis
morphology_keys.habit: Procumbent to ascending aquatic perennial, commonly mat-forming and rooting at nodes.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Opposite simple leaves, short-petioled; blades elliptic to obovate and generally glossy.
morphology_keys.flower: Small axillary yellow flower; morphology is typical of Ludwigia section Isnardia.
morphology_keys.joey_field_note: Joey's San Marcos River sequence shows the submerged/creeping form in situ, a useful contrast with the erect shoreline habit of Ludwigia octovalvis.

comparisons.key_distinctions: L. repens is low, creeping and node-rooting with opposite leaves; L. octovalvis is an erect, strongly ridged shoreline plant with alternate leaves and a conspicuously elongated inferior ovary. Hygrophila polysperma can mimic submerged L. repens, so confirm flower/fruit characters when possible.
